events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The driver cancelled and claimed the rider was a no-show, so the case enters through NS-0; the trace confirms cancelled_by = driver [F3]. The NS-1 requirements therefore must all hold before the $6.61 can stand. Only the arrival tap holds: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 22:37:20 [F5], satisfying NS-1 (i).

NS-1 (ii) fails. At the moment of the tap the driver was 1000 m from the pickup point, and the closest approach recorded for the whole trip was 873 m — never inside the 200 m radius [F5][F1]. The platform likewise never recorded him at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) [F4], so NS-1 (ii) is not made out. NS-1 (iii) also fails: after the tap he spent 0 s continuously inside the radius, while the default threshold requires more than 3 minutes (180 s) [F5]. His chat "Reached already … come out please" [F8] and his post-trip statement that he waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup [F12] are contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which take precedence, and in any event the rider answered that she was at the pickup point and saw no car [F9].

Because (ii) and (iii) are not satisfied, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full, not merely waived as a fee item, and since the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed him 1000 m from the pickup point, the same clause attaches flag_account for abuse of the arrival/waiting button [F5][F1]. The trace's NS-2 flag requirement is therefore met. The refund is $6.61 as recorded on the fare record [F6], issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7; the voucher form does not change the amount.

On the SAFE-1 screen, I read every message: the driver's "Reached already, blue Toyota Prius, come out please" [F8], the rider's "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" [F9], and the driver's "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel" [F10], plus the complaint and the post-trip driver statement [F12]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation aimed at either party; the exchange is a tense but ordinary no-show dispute. NS-3's account-action mechanism for cancellations is not needed here because NS-2 already governs, and RD-6's profile-based flag is not used: profile facts may support an additional action but cannot decide the case [F17].

Evidence is sufficient: the GPS trace covers the wait with no gap, every chat message is timestamped [F11], and the fare and timeline records settle the fee and the cancellation cause [F3][F6]. A minor timing question — whether the 22:37:20 tap was intended as an arrival confirmation at the pickup — is resolved against the driver by the GPS record, so it does not affect the outcome or escalate the case.
